source_hypotheses.required: The exact incoming assertions listed in this join.
source_hypotheses.constructed: For the actual D210 family, choose finite L-defined B-linear mu_sigma with mu_1=1. Their rational central discrepancies satisfy the cocycle identity; Tate functoriality holds for every ell. For rational discrepancy c, degree on rational quasi-isogenies and positive fourth roots give epsilon=c/|c|. No finite splitting is claimed by this result.
source_hypotheses.justification: The actual finite B-linear isogenies give c in Q*. Apply D(cu)=c^4D(u) and positive fourth roots to obtain a_sigma a_tau/a_sigma_tau=1/|c|, hence epsilon=c/|c|. Finite inflation of mu makes all scalars and epsilon factor through the original finite Galois quotient. Coefficients have trivial Galois action. This step does not split epsilon.
